files.description: Bike-share riders, one per row (400 rows): rider_id (six-digit id with leading zeros), display_name (person name, some with accented letters), home_district (one of 6 districts such as "Old Town"), membership (casual, monthly or annual) - these three text columns have inconsistent capital letters and stray spaces; joined_on (date as text, YYYY-MM-DD; about 2% empty), birth_year (whole number; about 4% empty), credit_balance (two decimals, can be negative; about 5% empty).

task_text: In riders.csv, find the five riders with the highest credit_balance in each membership level (membership trimmed and lower-cased), ignoring empty balances. `result` should be a table with columns membership, rider_id (text, leading zeros kept) and credit_balance, sorted by membership alphabetically, then credit_balance from highest to lowest, ties broken by rider_id.
intended_computation: Read riders.csv keeping rider_id as text; clean membership (strip, lower case); riders with a non-empty credit_balance; per membership the five highest balances (ties: smaller rider_id first); columns membership, rider_id, credit_balance; 15 rows sorted by membership ascending, credit_balance descending, rider_id ascending.

acceptable_variants.notes: id columns (rider_id, station codes) may be written as integers without leading zeros
